mobbin:06bcb061-a16d-4a6f-95bd-8c5e31c5f.summary: In an active huddle the user opens More, turns on push-to-talk, then gets a large hold-to-speak microphone control with clear muted versus live cues.
steps: Huddle More menu: turn on push-to-talk
Button held down; rings show it is live
steal: Push-to-talk is a mode you switch on under More (screen 1), so open mic versus hold-to-talk is a decision, not assumed.
A full-width muted push-to-talk screen with an X to leave (screen 2) shows you are not live before speaking.
An oversized bottom microphone button (screens 3 to 4) lets faculty who are gloved or holding gear hold to talk with one thumb.
A mute badge on the You tile plus the bottom control (screens 2 to 4) shows live or muted in two places.
avoid: Burying push-to-talk only under More (screen 1) is wrong for a dedicated room intercom; the mode should not require hunting in overflow.
mobbin:06bcb061-a16d-4a6f-95bd-8c5e31c5f.fit: Mobile and iPad app: the phone wins as an intercom microphone. Hold-to-talk with a large button reduces open-mic risk into a live sim room. This extends the baseline intercom, not the SRV.
